When to use: Use the Accordion to shorten a long page when the user only needs some of its sections: FAQ, help pages, settings groups, product details, order summaries. The headings give the overview and the user opens what they need. Related sections stack in an Accordion block, 3 to 6 sections at a time.

Do not hide what the user must see: a price, a warning, a required step or the main content of the page stays visible. For a single detail to expand inside a card, prefer a “Show more” link; for parallel content of equal importance, prefer tabs; for navigation, use plain links.
Layout: Heading
One short line that names the content, as a topic or as the question the user has in mind (“Shipping and returns”, “How do I cancel an order?”). Verbs like “Click to open” add nothing.
Indicator
The + / − indicator sits on the right and reflects the state; the icon on the left names the topic. Keep the same indicator across the product.
Open by default
Sections start closed, unless one of them answers the most common question: open that one. Several sections can stay open at once; opening a section never closes another.
Width
The accordion fills the width of its column. A heading wraps on two lines before it is shortened; the description keeps the width of the heading.

Do and don’t.do: Write headings that say what is inside
Do and don’t.doText: The user finds the section without opening it.
Do and don’t.dontText: Generic headings force the user to open every section.

Do and don’t.do: Group related sections in a block
Do and don’t.doText: One frame, one rhythm: the sections read as a list.
Do and don’t.dontText: Separate frames read as unrelated cards and double the borders.

Do and don’t.do: Open the most useful section by default
Do and don’t.doText: The common answer is visible at once; the rest stays one click away.
Do and don’t.dontText: The page is as long as without accordions, and the user has to close them.

notes: Contrast
Heading 19.8:1 (19.0:1 on the hover background), description 7.8:1, indicator 7.8:1.
Text must reach 4.5:1, icons 3:1.
Everything passes. The outline and the bottom rule (1.3:1) are decorative.
Icon size
The icon and the indicator are 14 × 14 px with a 1.4 px stroke.
The library has no size variable at 14 and no stroke variable; the rule elsewhere is 16 px (size/3xs), stroke 1.2 regular or 1.5 medium.
Align on 16 px and stroke 1.5 when the icon set is revised; the heading row stays 24 px high.
Block
The Accordion block holds five accordions and has no property.
Blocks of 3 to 6 sections are the common case, and hiding instances is manual.
Add show-item switches, as on the Dropdown, if blocks become frequent.
Content
The description is a single text.
Product accordions often hold lists, links, images or a form.
Swap the Description text for a slot frame when a screen needs richer content.

When to use: Use the Avatar wherever a person must be recognised at a glance: comment author, assignee, member list, message header, account menu in the Dropdown. Prefer the photo; fall back on the initials when the name is known, and keep the icon for an unknown or anonymous person and for the placeholder before a photo is uploaded.

Use the Avatar user when the name must be read, not only recognised: people pickers, member tables, assignee fields, profile headers. Use the Avatar group to show that several people share something (a project, a document, a thread): three or four faces and a counter, as a summary; the full list opens on click or in a tooltip.
Layout: Size
xs and sm in dense lists and tables, md in comments, cards and forms, lg and xl in profile headers. One size per context, and the same type for everyone in a list.
Status dot
Show presence only where it helps a decision (chat, calls, support). The dot never travels alone: a text, a tooltip or an accessible name gives the status in words.
Initials

First letter of the first name, then of the last name, in uppercase; one letter when only one name is known. All initials share the brand colour: a colour per person adds nothing the name does not already say.
Group
The most important or most recent person comes first, on top of the stack. Beyond four, the counter takes over, and a click gives access to the full list.

Do and don’t.do: Fall back on initials when there is no photo
Do and don’t.doText: The initials still identify the person.
Do and don’t.dont: Show the generic icon for a known person
Do and don’t.dontText: The icon says nothing about who it is.

Do and don’t.do: Give the status in words next to the dot
Do and don’t.doText: The status is read, not guessed from a colour.
Do and don’t.dont: Let the dot alone carry the status
Do and don’t.dontText: Busy, in a call and do not disturb share the same red.

Do and don’t.do: Summarise a group with a counter
Do and don’t.doText: Four faces and a count tell the story.
Do and don’t.dontText: A long row takes space and still cannot be read.

notes: _Avatar add
The _Avatar add set (state × size) is no longer on any page: the Add button of the Avatar group still points to it, but it cannot be edited or published.
No component is created without agreement.
Restore it from the version history, or bring it back on this page before the next publish.
Out-of-office pink
No semantic pink token: the out-of-office dot is bound to the primitive colors/pink/500.
No variable is created without agreement.
Add a token such as background/system/presence/out-of-office, or pick an existing colour.
Dot sizes
8, 10 and 14 px have no variable; only 12 px (size/4xs) and 16 px (size/3xs) are bound.
The size scale starts at 12 px.
Add sizes under 12 px, or keep these values fixed in the component.
Do-not-disturb bar
The white bar is 60 % of the dot, a fixed length; its thickness is bound to border/xs or border/sm.
No variable matches such a short length.
Keep it fixed: it is a drawing detail.
Status and colour
busy and in-call share the same red, as requested, and the status is carried by colour only.
Information must not rely on colour alone.
In code, give the status as text (tooltip and accessible name).
Contrast

Dots on the white ring: green 3.3:1, amber 3.2:1, red 3.8:1, grey 4.7:1 (bold versions chosen; the base green and amber were 2.3:1 and 2.1:1). Initials 5.5:1 (4.8:1 in Dark), icon 5.5:1, detail 7.8:1, counter 9.5:1.
Text must reach 4.5:1, graphics 3:1.
Everything passes in Light and Dark.
Demo photo
The photo comes from randomuser.me.
It is only a placeholder.
Replace it with a licensed photo before any publication.
Group overlap
The overlap between avatars is a fixed negative gap: −4, −6, −8, −10 and −12 px by size.
There is no negative spacing variable.
Add negative values to 3c. semantic.layout, or keep them fixed.

When to use: Use the Alert for feedback that concerns a page or a section and stays until the user acts or dismisses it: a failed payment, a saved draft, a plan about to expire, a step to complete. It sits in the content, at the top of the page or of the form, under the heading.

For a message about one field, use the Hint of the Input. For a message that concerns the whole site (maintenance, outage, policy), use the Banner. To label a state in a few words without talking to the user, use the Badge. For a short confirmation that needs no action, a toast is the better fit; it is not in the library yet.
Layout: Status

information for a neutral fact, success for a completed action, warning for something to check before it becomes a problem, error for something that failed and needs an action. One alert at a time per section; the most severe wins.
Writing
The title says what happened in a few words; the description says what it means and what to do. The action names the next step (Retry, Update card, Open drafts), never OK or Close.
Placement
Top of the page content or of the form, under the heading, as wide as its column (Fill). An alert that answers a submit replaces the previous one and receives focus or is announced.
Dismiss
Show the cross only when the message is not needed to finish the task. A blocking error stays until it is fixed; a success message can go away on its own after a few seconds, or on the cross.

Do and don’t.do: Say what happened and what to do next
Do and don’t.doText: The title names the problem, the description the fix, the action the next step.
Do and don’t.dont: Leave the user without a next step
Do and don’t.dontText: A generic message and no action: the user does not know what to do.

Do and don’t.doText: A deadline is a warning: it can still be handled.
Do and don’t.dontText: Red for something that has not failed makes real errors invisible.

Do and don’t.do: Keep a blocking error on screen
Do and don’t.doText: The message stays until the situation is fixed.
Do and don’t.dont: Let a blocking error be dismissed
Do and don’t.dontText: Once closed, the user has lost the reason the form is stuck.

notes: Action in Dark
Brand ghost Button. In Light, 4.9 to 5.4:1 on the tinted backgrounds. In Dark, 2.6 to 3.3:1.
Button text must reach 4.5:1.
Lighten text/brand/base in Dark, or force the Light mode on the alert. With filled=False everything passes.
Description in Dark
text/neutral/base on the tinted backgrounds: 5.4 to 6.8:1 in Dark, 8.5 to 9.4:1 in Light.
Text must reach 4.5:1.
Same fix as the action if a value falls under 4.5:1.
Icon colour
Icons in icon/system/…/bold: 3.4 to 5.3:1 on the tinted backgrounds, at least 3.9:1 on white. The base version was too light (2.5:1 for information).
A meaningful icon must reach 3:1.
Keep bold.
Link component
The action is a ghost Button for now.
The library has no Link component yet.
Replace it with the Link when it exists.
One icon property per status
icon-information, icon-success, icon-warning and icon-error; only the one of the current status shows in the panel.
A shared property would have one default icon for every variant.
Keep as is.
Width
400 px by default.
The alert must follow its container.
In screens, set the instance to Fill width.

When to use: Use the Badge to label a state or a category in one or two words, right next to what it qualifies: an order status in a table row, New beside an item of the Dropdown, Beta on a feature, the plan level in the account header. It is scanned in a list and read in a sentence; it is never clicked.

To talk to the user about something that happened, use the Alert. For a count on an icon (unread messages) or a tag the user can add and remove, a different component is needed; neither is in the library yet.
Layout: Wording
One or two words, a noun or a past participle: Paid, In review, Draft, Archived, New. No verb, no sentence, no punctuation. The same word always means the same thing across the product.
Status
information for a neutral state or a category, success for done or active, warning for pending or needing attention, error for failed, blocked or expired. One colour per meaning, everywhere.
Size
sm in dense tables and menus, md by default in cards and lists, lg next to a page title. One size per context.
Icon
Optional. Keep it when it helps to tell the statuses apart at a glance, and make the same choice for every badge of a list.

Do and don’t.doText: The badge is read at a glance.
Do and don’t.dontText: A long label is a message: that is an Alert.

Do and don’t.doText: Paid is green, pending amber, failed red, everywhere.
Do and don’t.dontText: The same words in other colours break the code the user has learnt.

Do and don’t.do: The same icon choice in a list
Do and don’t.doText: Every badge of the list has an icon, or none has.
Do and don’t.dontText: The odd one out looks like a different state.

notes: Text colour
Label in text/system/…/stronger: 7.0 to 8.3:1 in Light, 7.0 to 8.3:1 in Dark. The bold version failed on the tinted background (3.4:1 for information).
Text must reach 4.5:1.
Keep stronger.
Icon colour
Icons in icon/system/…/bold: 3.4 to 5.3:1 on the tinted backgrounds.
A meaningful icon must reach 3:1.
Keep bold; the word carries the meaning anyway.
Background on white
The tinted backgrounds sit at 1.1 to 1.2:1 on white.
Only the text has to pass; the tint is decorative.
Nothing to do.
Radius in Sylva
radius/sm and radius/md are 1 px in Sylva.
Brand choice made earlier.
Keep as is.
One icon property per status
icon-information, icon-success, icon-warning and icon-error; only the one of the current status shows in the panel.
A shared property would have one default icon for every variant.
Keep as is.

When to use: Use the Banner for a message that concerns the whole site or the whole account and that every page must show while the situation lasts: planned maintenance, an outage, a payment problem on the account, a policy change, a new version to adopt. It sits at the very top of the screen, above the header, over the full width.

For feedback about one page, one section or one form, use the Alert. For a state in one or two words, use the Badge. A banner is rare by nature: if the product shows one every day, the message belongs somewhere else.
Layout: Status

information for an announcement or a maintenance; warning for something to do before a date (payment method, email to verify); error for a degraded service or a suspended account; success rarely, for a migration or an upgrade that is done.
One banner
One banner at a time, the most severe first. The next one shows when the first is closed or the situation ends.
Writing
A short title, one sentence of description, and an action that fixes the situation (Update payment method, See status page). No cross when the user cannot do without the message.
Persistence
The banner stays on every page until the situation ends or the user closes it; a dismissal is remembered for the session at least, so the banner does not come back on the next page.

Do and don’t.do: A message about the whole site
Do and don’t.doText: Maintenance concerns every page: the banner is the right place.
Do and don’t.dontText: A saved draft concerns one page: that is an Alert.

Do and don’t.doText: The most severe message first; the next waits.
Do and don’t.dontText: Two or three banners push the content down and cancel each other.

Do and don’t.do: An action that fixes the situation
Do and don’t.doText: The user knows what to do and the banner can go away.
Do and don’t.dont: A message with no way out
Do and don’t.dontText: Without an action or a cross, the banner stays for ever and says nothing new.

notes: Strong colours and contrast
error in bold (4.8:1) and warning in base with dark text (4.8:1). information and success use stronger (5.9:1 and 7.1:1); their bold version with white text fell to 2.8:1 and 3.3:1.
Text must reach 4.5:1.
A brighter blue or green would need dark text on those two statuses.
Light mode forced
The component is locked in Light mode on the 3a. semantic.color collection.
In Dark, the stronger backgrounds would turn pale and the white text unreadable.
Keep as is: a site notice looks the same whatever the theme.
Width
1440 px by default; 1200 px in this documentation.
The banner must take the full width of the screen.
In screens, set the instance to Fill width.
Action
Ghost Button in static white or static black for now.
The library has no Link component yet.
Replace it with the Link when it exists.

When to use: Use the Breadcrumb on pages that sit at least two levels below the root of a hierarchy: a catalogue, a documentation, settings, a file tree. It sits under the header and above the page title, as a secondary navigation. It shows the path from the root to the page, not the history of the visit.
Not on the home page, not on a flat site, and never as a replacement for the main navigation or for the browser back button. The hidden levels of a long path open in the Dropdown behind the ellipsis.
Layout: Levels
Two to four levels are shown in full. From five, keep the root and the current page and collapse the levels between behind the ellipsis.
Labels
The page titles, as they appear in the navigation: short nouns, no verbs. A long title is cut at about twenty characters, with the full title in a tooltip.
Current page
Always last, in medium weight, and not a link. On small screens the breadcrumb can shrink to a single link back to the parent.
Icons
Optional and the same choice on every level: house for the root, folder for the levels between, document for the page. Without icons, the path is lighter.

Do and don’t.do: Collapse the middle levels beyond four
Do and don’t.doText: The root and the page stay visible; the rest is one click away.
Do and don’t.dont: Show six levels in a row
Do and don’t.dontText: A long path is hard to scan and wraps on small screens.

Do and don’t.doText: The path reads like the navigation.
Do and don’t.dontText: A verb or a long label is not a place in the site.

Do and don’t.do: End with the current page, not a link
Do and don’t.doText: The user knows where they are; nothing to click.
Do and don’t.dont: Make the current page a link
Do and don’t.dontText: A link to the page the user is already on goes nowhere.

notes: Contrast
Links 7.8:1, current page 19.8:1, ellipsis 7.8:1, chevrons 2.5:1.
Text must reach 4.5:1, meaningful icons 3:1.
Everything passes; the chevrons are decorative.
Hidden levels menu
The ellipsis opens an instance of the Dropdown (sm) with three items and no icon.
One component for every drop-down list.
Set the items from the Dropdown instance inside the ellipsis.
Collapse rule
The 5+ variant is chosen by hand from five levels.
Figma cannot count the levels for the designer.
In code, beyond four levels, show the root, the ellipsis and the current page.
Link height
Links are 20 px high, with no vertical padding.
The breadcrumb must stay compact.
In code, extend the hit area to 24 px without changing the look.
